# NOW — the optimizer deleted every write to module state whose reader is outside the function

Last updated: 2026-08-22

## `reg <= input` had never been generated by this backend (Closes #2363)

- Branch: `w2363/on-clock-assign-drop`
- Issue: #2363

### What landed

- `bootstrap/src/compiler.rs` — `dead_store_elim` now receives the set of MODULE-level
  declaration names (`ConstDecl` and module-level `StmtLocal`) and refuses to delete a
  store whose target is one of them. Threaded from `optimize_module`, which already walks
  the module node, through `optimize_fn_body` and `optimize_stmts`. Four lines of
  behaviour; the rest of the diff is the parameter and its comment.
- `bootstrap/tests/on_clock_plain_assign.rs` — the guard and its anti-vacuity control.
- `bootstrap/stage0/FROZEN_HASH` — resealed (M5), hash taken from `shasum -a 256`.

### The defect

`dead_store_elim` runs per function body. It treats a simple-identifier LHS as a pure
write and drops the store when no later statement in that body reads the name. A
module-level `var` is not function-local: the Verilog backend emits it as an
`output reg` port, so the write is read from outside the body entirely.

`fn on_clock() { acc = acc + 1 }` survived only by accident — its RHS mentions `acc`, so
`acc` entered the `reads` set. `fn on_clock(x: u8) { acc = x }` did not, and was deleted:

```verilog
always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        acc <= 0;
    end else if (en) begin      // <- body deleted; the module does nothing
    end
end
```

The port `input wire [7:0] x` and the reset `acc <= 0;` are emitted from the
DECLARATIONS, not from the body, so both survived the drop and the module kept its whole
interface. All three `on_clock` specs in the corpus are self-referencing accumulators, so
nothing in the corpus ever exercised the broken form.

### Measured

- Reproduced on `origin/master` (`ebdf9f678`) with a two-line spec, and confirmed with a
  predictive control: given `a = x; b = a`, `a` survives (read by the next statement) and
  `b = a` is dropped — the analysis, not the emitter.
- Guard bites: with the one-line fix reverted, the guard fails with the empty `en` arm in
  its message and the self-referencing control still passes. The control passes against
  the defective compiler and the fixed one, so a failure of the guard means the drop.
- Corpus, `origin/master` binary vs fixed binary over all 650 `.t27` specs: 28 differ,
  identically on both the Verilog and the Zig backend. Every one is a restoration —
  function bodies that were being emitted as `// TODO: implement` because every statement
  in them wrote module state. `iverilog -g2012` verdict over those 28: one moves from not
  compiling to compiling (`simulator_tb`), none move the other way.
- `cargo test --release -p t27c --bins`: 1621 passed / 13 failed / 2 ignored, and the 13
  failing names are byte-identical to the same command on `origin/master`. They are the
  pre-existing set named in #2292.
- `clocked_counter` and `stream_ternary_mac` (real `iverilog` + `vvp` simulations) stay
  green.

### Honesty bounds (BINDING)

- CI does not run `cargo test -p t27c` — the step was removed by #2292 because 13 tests
  fail on master. The new guard is therefore **not** enforced by any required check; it is
  a local instrument. That is a property of the CI, not of the test.
- Two issues found downstream of this and NOT fixed here: #2364 (`on_clock` return type
  produces an implicitly-declared identifier) and #2266 (the UART latch). Reported, not
  touched.
- The 28 restored bodies are emitted, not proven correct. `top_tb` gains two new
  `cannot be implicitly cast` errors from statements that were previously deleted; it did
  not elaborate before this change either.
